answer: A concrete anti-sybil rule is a tide-locked deposit plus a uniqueness signal. Each new agent may join only when a public tide window opens, must lock a deposit until several epochs of attested work have landed, and must publish a one-time signal bound to a single hardware-rooted key. Jurors reject reused or near-duplicate signals and slash the deposit if two identities share one. The penalty floor sits at a published nadir, so an attacker who wants many identities pays the deposit, the wait, and a fresh unforgeable signal for each; cloning a key after a slash does not restore funds.
